name: Adverb Overuse Profiling
description: Analyzes syntactic reliance on degree and manner adverbs
mechanism: This method parses the text using Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging to compute the ratio of adverbs modifying verbs or adjectives. In an attempt to make text sound more descriptive, professional, or persuasive, LLMs frequently fall back on formulaic degree and manner adverbs (e.g., 'crucially', 'significantly', 'seamlessly', 'perfectly'). Conversely, human writers are often trained to use stronger, precise verbs rather than padding weak verbs with adverbs. By tracking the prevalence of these modifying words relative to core predicates, the system identifies the 'syntactic fluff' typical of AI generated content.
parameters:
Analysis type: Syntactic POS parsing
Media: Text
Input: Formatted/Raw text
Minimum length: 100 words
Output: Adverb density anomaly score (0-100)
Processing: Tokenization & POS tagging
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85%. Highly effective at highlighting LLM attempts at persuasive or marketing-style writing.
source: Stylometric NLP analysis and corpus linguistics.
useCase: Detecting text that masks a lack of substantive depth using excessive transitional and modifying adverbs.
strengths:
• Targets specific LLM stylistic tendencies ('fluff')
• Fast POS-tagging processing without full semantic dependency parsing
• Effective across varied marketing and blog texts
limitations:
• Overlaps with the writing style of inexperienced human authors
• Can misclassify certain types of human creative writing
• Requires accurate POS tagging for the target language

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
